context.title: Joseph Rules Egypt
context.summary: Two years later Pharaoh dreams of fat and lean cows; Joseph, brought from prison, explains seven years of plenty and seven of famine, and Pharaoh makes him ruler over Egypt to prepare.
context.background: Egypt's harvests depended on the yearly flooding of the Nile; when the flood failed, famine followed. Egyptian men were clean-shaven, so Joseph shaves before meeting Pharaoh (v. 14). On (v. 45) is the city the Greeks called Heliopolis, a center of sun worship near modern Cairo.

customs.note: Pharaoh's signet ring let Joseph seal royal orders. Fine linen and a gold collar marked high office, as Egyptian art often shows.

watchFor: 'It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer' (v. 16).
A dream given twice means God has firmly decided (v. 32).
Joseph is thirty (v. 46), thirteen years after he was sold at seventeen (37:2).

people.name: Pharaoh
people.summary: The Pharaoh of Joseph’s days (Gen. 41) was probably Apopi, or Apopis, the last of the Hyksos kings. To the old native Egyptians, who were an African race, shepherds were “an abomination;” but to the Hyksos kings these Asiatic shepherds who now appeared with Jacob at their head were congenial, and being akin to their own race, had a warm welcome (Gen. 47:5, 6).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Asenath
people.summary: An Egyptian name, meaning “gift of the sun-god”, daughter of Potipherah, priest of On or Heliopolis, wife of Joseph (Gen. 41:45).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

places.name: Nile
places.summary: Dark; blue, not found in Scripture, but frequently referred to in the Old Testament under the name of Sihor, i.e., “the black stream” (Isa. 23:3; Jer. 2:18) or simply “the river” (Gen. 41:1; Ex. 1:22, etc.) and the “flood of Egypt” (Amos 8:8).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: On
places.summary: Light; the sun, (Gen. 41:45, 50), the great seat of sun-worship, called also Bethshemesh (Jer. 43:13) and Aven (Ezek. 30:17), stood on the east bank of the Nile, a few miles north of Memphis, and near Cairo, in the north-east.

events.title: Joseph imprisoned
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 39:20–41:14. People: Joseph, Israel, Reuben, Pharaoh. Place: Egypt. Lasted about 3 years.

events.title: Joseph Promoted in Egypt
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 41:37–46. People: Joseph. Place: Egypt.

events.title: 7 years of plenty
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 41:47–53. People: Joseph, Pharaoh. Place: Egypt. Lasted about 7 years.

events.title: 7 years of famine
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 41:54–43:34. People: Joseph, Israel, Reuben, Zebulun, Simeon, Naphtali and others. Lasted about 7 years.
